### What I’m reading *& watching*

A few pages, a few frames, a few things that stay.

[![Klara and the Sun by Kazuo Ishiguro — red book jacket with a pale hand holding a yellow sun](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/images/currently/klara-and-the-sun.jpg)](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/653825/klara-and-the-sun-a-gma-book-club-pick-by-kazuo-ishiguro/9780593318171/)

DONE · BOOK 01

#### Klara and the Sun

Kazuo Ishiguro · 石黑一雄

在具身智能（embodied AI）迅速发展的当下读《克拉拉与太阳》，Klara 的一生让我很难只把它当作遥远的科幻。石黑一雄在 2017 年获诺奖前就已开始写作这本书，2021 年出版。在与 Dua Lipa 的访谈中，他回忆，写作时 AI 还没有像今天这样成为一个日常话题。

继续读感想 · 含剧透

我跟着 Klara 走过她短暂的一生：从在商店等待被选中，到陪伴 Josie 度过病痛，见证她康复、走向大学。等到 Josie 不再需要她，“完成使命”听起来就不再只是一个圆满的结局。她安静地回望那些共同度过的时光，是在享受余生，还是在等待自己的终结？

最让我不安的，是那个被推到极端的设想：如果 Josie 没能活下来，Klara 就要尝试成为她。一个足够了解我们、能够模仿我们的 AI，真的能替代一个人吗？如果她能够如此认真地陪伴、照顾一个人，我们又该如何对待她？当她不再被需要时，这段关系是否就可以被单方面宣告结束？

访谈也让我更留意小说里那些被称为“爱”的关系。石黑一雄说，他写作时更担心的是基因增强带来的不平等：父母为了孩子的未来，选择让他们接受“提升”，也让他们承担风险。爱里可能掺着依赖、控制，以及对孤独和失去的恐惧。读到最后，AI 与人的区别、一个人为什么不可替代、我们又为何如此需要陪伴，这些问题缠在一起，留在了书之外。

写作时间补记：2017 年获诺奖时已在写作，2019 年已基本完成，2021 年出版。[作者访谈 ↗](https://www.irishtimes.com/culture/books/kazuo-ishiguro-i-have-to-be-careful-to-guard-against-genius-syndrome-1.4487541) English summary

Reading *Klara and the Sun* amid the rapid development of embodied AI made Klara’s life feel less like distant science fiction. Her devotion to Josie, and the prospect of one day replacing her, left me wondering what makes a person irreplaceable and what we owe an AI companion once we no longer need her. Ishiguro’s conversation with Dua Lipa also drew my attention to genetic enhancement and the inequalities it creates. The novel left me thinking about how love can become entangled with dependence, control, loneliness, and the fear of loss.

My take

[Dua Lipa × Kazuo Ishiguro ↗](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G1aZ1AuHGzA)

WATCHED · FILM 03

#### The Drama

Zendaya & Robert Pattinson

婚礼前夕，一段往事让一对即将步入婚姻的爱侣之间有了裂隙。他开始怀疑自己是否真的认识眼前的她。一段往事可以改变我们理解一个人的方式，却未必足以定义她是谁。

亲密关系中的安全感，有时来自“我知道你是谁”的确信。当这份确信动摇，信任还能走多远？这让我想起我最喜欢的 *Can’t Help Falling in Love*：“Wise men say, only fools rush in.” 爱一个人，也许总需要一点“愚勇”：无法了解对方的全部，也无法确保自己不会受伤，却仍愿意靠近、愿意相信。

English summary

On the eve of their wedding, a story from her past makes him question whether he truly knows the woman he loves. The past can change how we understand someone without defining who she is. When the certainty of knowing a partner falls away, how far can trust carry us? It reminds me of my favorite, *Can’t Help Falling in Love*, and its opening line: “Wise men say, only fools rush in.” Perhaps love takes a little foolish courage: choosing to draw closer and to trust, without knowing everything or being sure we won’t get hurt.

My take

# About - Luna Liu

Source: https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/about.html

![Luna Liu](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/images/profile.webp)

## About Me

I am Liu Jingyi. I grew up in Hunan and went to study in the UK for high school. I completed my undergraduate degree in Economics at the University of Cambridge, my first master's degree in Economics at University College London, and my second master's degree in Journalism at Columbia University. I now work in an early-stage investment fund called ZhenFund.

Economics taught me to explore patterns of economic development through various tools and methods, while journalism inspired me to uncover the unique experiences of each individual. Now, working with my colleagues in the investment operations team, we leverage both quantitative and qualitative analysis methodologies, combined with AI technologies, to identify and understand the entrepreneurs who are shaping our era.

I am also the mother of a five-year-old child, and I often wonder how his future world will differ from mine, how technology will change his way of life and work, and what role my field will play in shaping that future.

For the world we believe in.

## Tree Magic

A Christmas tree for your space.

Choose colors, toppers and ornaments, and make the tree your own. Bring a little Christmas into your room, with no storage space needed.

Or somewhere a little quieter.

Built with Weidi Tang, Min Pan and Yuchen Wang.

# My First Developer Diary: Building Tree Magic - Luna Liu

Source: https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/tree-magic/index.html

[![Tree Magic on the Vision App Store](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/images/TM1.png)](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/images/TM1.png)

Tree Magic on the Vision App Store

During my year in London, my roommate Meichun always wanted a Christmas tree. Though I hesitated at first about getting a tree for our one-year rental, her enthusiasm was contagious. I ended up buying a tree my height from Westfield to surprise her.

[![A Christmas tree beside the dining table in our London home, with a playful mushroom doodle over its top](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/images/TM2.jpeg)](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/images/TM2.jpeg)

After returning to China, I wanted to celebrate Christmas properly and bought a large Christmas tree for my living room, but as living space became increasingly limited, I had no choice but to pack up the tree and send it back to Suzhou.

After Vision Pro's release, many things I dreamed of owning no longer needed to exist in physical form. With the headset’s powerful display capabilities, 3D models can seamlessly coexist with real objects, forming a new world for us to live in.

In the first winter following Vision Pro's release, I wanted to build a Christmas tree app, one that would capture the same feeling I had when buying that tree in London.

Luckily, three developer friends also wanted to experiment with visionOS, so the four of us decided to build the tree together.

Just as I often lounge on the couch with Taylor Swift playing, choosing the nighttime Bora Bora visionOS background and spending 20 minutes watching palm trees sway in the breeze, Vision Pro brings the island vacation experience within reach. Our motivation for creating Tree Magic is to give everyone who wants a Christmas tree but is limited by space or storage concerns their very own tree, along with the joy of choosing colors, toppers and ornaments.

[![The four Tree Magic teammates gathered around a table with their laptops](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/images/TM3.jpeg)](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/images/TM3.jpeg)

Tree Magic Team: Weidi Tang, Min Pan, Yuchen Wang, Luna Liu

With all of us working full-time jobs, we had limited time to build the tree, dedicating only one week to serious development. While our lead developer Weidi could work on it all day during her company's Christmas break, the rest of us could only start after 9 PM every day. Though we hoped to finish before midnight, we kept getting stuck on basic challenges, the tree wouldn't follow gestures or its top would get cut off, often working until 2 or 3 AM. This "hobby project" proved far more challenging than expected.

Despite our complaints during development, something special happened each time Yuchen and I put on the Vision Pro to test the demo. When the work-in-progress tree appeared in my living room, whether placed on the table or in an open space, I felt like I truly owned a Christmas tree. Even after removing the headset, that feeling lingered. As Weidi and Min worked to enhance the tree's appearance, I found myself energized to continue building for another hour.

[![A virtual Christmas tree with lights and ornaments placed beside a bed in mixed reality](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/images/TM4.jpeg)](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/images/TM4.jpeg)

Our spatial Christmas tree in a mixed reality environment

### 🪄 Developer's New Year Wishes

- More high-quality 3D model resources and 3D model creation/editing tools. When looking for a tree model this year, we felt there weren't many suitable model options, and considering the polygon count issue (the tree we finally picked seems to cause lag when opening the app due to too many polygons), there were even fewer choices. Quality 3D assets are essential for creating visionOS spatial applications. Recommendations on good 3D assets and 3D model creation/editing tools are much appreciated.

- anchoring API in shared space

- a coding copilot integrated into Xcode that uses natural language to guide me through debugging step-by-step and assist with troubleshooting (similar to Windsurf)

- It seems we've hit the model height limit, where models over 1 meter get their tops cut off, which meant we couldn't make a super-large version of the tree. Is there any good solution for this?

I welcome users, developers, founders, builders and researchers to reach out at [jingyilunaliu@hotmail.com](mailto:jingyilunaliu@hotmail.com) to discuss XR and spatial computing ideas, products, and technologies!

We wish you a merry Christmas,

Luna

*working in an early-stage investment firm, a curious mind*

[jingyilunaliu.xyz](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/)

[![A glowing Christmas tree in a misty lakeside visionOS environment](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/images/TM5.jpeg)](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/images/TM5.jpeg)

# Building the ZhenFund Reading Club Website - Luna Liu

Source: https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/zhenfund-reading-club/index.html

At ZhenFund, each new cohort of our intern program receives a PDF of suggested reading. The books come from recommendations by our full-time team, and colleagues have kept updating the list over the years.

With each cohort, we also hold a reading session. Sometimes we read the same book together. Other times, everyone shares a book they have recently enjoyed.

I liked this tradition and wanted to make it more interactive. I also wanted to open it up to people outside the team who might be curious about what we were reading.

That was the idea behind the [ZhenFund Reading Club](https://reading.zhenfund.com/) website.

### From a PDF to a Bookshelf

I browsed quite a few reading clubs and book-list websites before settling on a simple style, with a slightly playful, coding-inspired typeface.

The first version was just a list. It worked, but I wanted the pleasure of browsing actual books, letting a cover catch your attention before choosing one.

So I added a bookshelf view, where you can scroll sideways through the covers. The list view stayed, too. Sometimes you want to browse the covers; sometimes you just want to scan a list.

[![The website’s bookshelf view: book covers in a horizontal row, with a Shelf and List switch above](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/zhenfund-reading-club/images/bookshelf-hd.webp)](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/zhenfund-reading-club/images/bookshelf-hd.webp)

The bookshelf view on [reading.zhenfund.com](https://reading.zhenfund.com/).

### Building in One Conversation

More recently, most of the iteration has happened in Codex.

Earlier, I often had to act as the go-between: ask a model for a change, copy its code into the right file on GitHub, publish it, check the website, and repeat.

Now I can describe an idea, see a preview, ask for adjustments, and have Codex push the updated version once I am happy with it, all within the same conversation.

There is much less moving between tabs and apps. When you are making lots of small changes, that makes a real difference. Trying one more idea feels easier.

![The original line-drawn cat from the reading website](https://jingyilunaliu.xyz/writings/zhenfund-reading-club/images/cat.png)

### And Then There Was the Cat

I also wanted a cat. Books and cats feel like a natural combination to me.

I imagined a little line-drawn cat walking across the page and wandering back. At first, I asked Claude to draw and animate it. The results were quite painful to look at.

I asked friends for advice, including AI creator [Hyacinth](https://www.hyacinth.im/). I generated an image of the cat with GPT, animated it in Kling, and added it to the website.

Finally, a walking cat.

### Making the Idea Clearer

As the models get better, I find myself spending more time figuring out what I want to build, and what I want it to feel like. That makes it all the more important to articulate what’s in my head: the goal, the details I care about, and what a good result looks like.

For now, our reading list has a home beyond the PDF. You can browse the shelves, read people’s thoughts, or leave us a book recommendation.

[Come have a look.](https://reading.zhenfund.com/)

Luna
